title: Hermione Lee: Biography is a dying art
gist: In an interview, biographer Hermione Lee says biography may be a dying art as self-publicisation leaves fewer secrets, and argues that biography should look at circumstances and character rather than assigning blame.

insights.claim: Hermione Lee suspects biography as she practises it may no longer be widely read, partly because self-publicisation means personal details once hidden are now freely revealed.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stephen
insights.so_what: Cultural signal on declining demand for long-form literary biography.
insights.quote: I don’t know whether biography the way I do it is going to be read much… maybe it’s gone.

insights.claim: Lee begins research by tracing her subject's footsteps before archives, and her Stoppard research involved tracking down his dentist, accountant, hairdresser and children's nanny.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stephen

insights.claim: Lee argues biographers wrongly ask 'who is to blame?' of tragedies, preferring circumstances, serendipity and character.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stephen
insights.so_what: Framing of life narratives without punitive fault-finding.
